broker-rolling-restart — Kafka Broker Rolling Restart Procedure

# Kafka Broker Rolling Restart Procedure

Version 4 · Effective 2026-04-01 · Owner: Streaming SRE

## When to use this procedure

Use this procedure to restart every broker in the production cluster one at a
time, for config changes, OS patching or a Kafka upgrade. Never restart more
than one broker at a time.

## Before you start

- Change record: use the pre-approved standard change template `STD-KAFKA-ROLL`.
- Window: **Wednesday 14:00–17:00 UTC**.
- Pre-check: under-replicated partitions = 0 and under-min-ISR partitions = 0.

## Steps

1. Restart brokers in this order: all non-controller brokers by ascending id, the active controller last.
2. Restart the broker with: `kctl broker restart --id <n>`.
3. Allow controlled shutdown up to **180 seconds** before forcing it.
4. Wait **10 minutes** after the broker rejoins, then re-run the pre-check.
5. Move to the next broker only when the pre-check passes again.

## Abort

If a pre-check fails twice in a row, stop and page the on-call.

# Kafka Broker Rolling Restart Procedure

Version 3 · Effective 2025-03-10 · Owner: Data Platform

## When to use this procedure

Use this procedure to restart every broker in the production cluster one at a
time, for config changes, OS patching or a Kafka upgrade. Never restart more
than one broker at a time.

## Before you start

- Change record: raise a normal change and get CAB approval.
- Window: **Tuesday or Thursday 22:00–02:00 UTC**.
- Pre-check: under-replicated partitions = 0.

## Steps

1. Restart brokers in this order: by ascending broker id.
2. Restart the broker with: `sudo systemctl restart kafka`.
3. Allow controlled shutdown up to **60 seconds** before forcing it.
4. Wait **5 minutes** after the broker rejoins, then re-run the pre-check.
5. Move to the next broker only when the pre-check passes again.

## Abort

If a pre-check fails twice in a row, stop and page the on-call.

chunks.heading: Kafka Consumer Lag Alerting Runbook
chunks.text:
consumer-lag-alerting — Kafka Consumer Lag Alerting Runbook

# Kafka Consumer Lag Alerting Runbook

Version 2 · Effective 2026-03-01 · Owner: Streaming SRE

## When to use this runbook

Use this runbook when a consumer group on the production cluster falls behind
its topics. It defines the alert thresholds, where the alert comes from, and the
first actions on-call takes.

## Alert thresholds

- **Warning:** consumer lag above 5 minutes of time lag for 5 minutes. Posts to the team channel only.
- **Page:** consumer lag above 10 minutes of time lag for 5 minutes. Pages the primary on-call.
- Consumer groups whose name starts with `test-` or `tmp-` never alert.

## Where the numbers come from

Lag is collected by **kafka-lag-exporter**, which exposes metrics on port **9308**.
The alert rule reads the metric `kafka_consumergroup_lag_seconds`. The dashboard is **Kafka Consumer Health**
in Grafana.

## First response

chunks.heading: First response
chunks.text:
consumer-lag-alerting — First response

## First response

1. Open the dashboard and confirm which partitions are behind.
2. Check that the consumer pods are running: `kubectl get pods -l app=<group>`.
3. Scale the consumer deployment out, up to twice its normal replica count.
4. If lag is still growing after 20 minutes, follow the on-call escalation runbook.

chunks.text:
consumer-lag-alerting-2024 — Kafka Consumer Lag Alerting Runbook

# Kafka Consumer Lag Alerting Runbook

Version 1 · Effective 2024-06-01 · Owner: Data Platform

## When to use this runbook

Use this runbook when a consumer group on the production cluster falls behind
its topics. It defines the alert thresholds, where the alert comes from, and the
first actions on-call takes.

## Alert thresholds

- **Warning:** consumer lag above 50,000 messages for 5 minutes. Posts to the team channel only.
- **Page:** consumer lag above 100,000 messages for 5 minutes. Pages the primary on-call.
- Consumer groups whose name starts with `test-` or `tmp-` never alert.

## Where the numbers come from

Lag is collected by **lag-monitor**, which exposes metrics on port **9999**.
The alert rule reads the metric `kafka_consumergroup_lag`. The dashboard is **Kafka Lag (legacy)**
in Grafana.

## First response

1. Open the dashboard and confirm which partitions are behind.
2. Check that the consumer pods are running: `kubectl get pods -l app=<group>`.
3. Restart the consumer deployment with `kubectl rollout restart`.
4. If lag is still growing after 20 minutes, follow the on-call escalation runbook.

chunks.heading: Kafka Broker Disk Capacity Runbook
chunks.text:
disk-capacity — Kafka Broker Disk Capacity Runbook

# Kafka Broker Disk Capacity Runbook

Version 3 · Effective 2026-05-01 · Owner: Streaming SRE

## Scope

Disk usage on the Kafka data volume `/var/lib/kafka` on every production
broker.

## Alert thresholds

- **Warning** at **75%** used.
- **Page** at **85%** used.
- **Emergency** at **92%** used: stop all non-critical producers.

## First response

1. Find the largest topics: `du -sh /var/lib/kafka/* | sort -h | tail`.
2. Lower retention on the three largest topics with `kctl topic set-retention`. Never delete segment files by hand.
3. If usage is still rising, expand the volume by **1 TiB**.

## Capacity review

Disk headroom is reviewed **monthly** with the infrastructure team.

disk-capacity-2025 — Kafka Broker Disk Capacity Runbook

# Kafka Broker Disk Capacity Runbook

Version 2 · Effective 2025-02-01 · Owner: Data Platform

## Scope

Disk usage on the Kafka data volume `/var/lib/kafka` on every production
broker.

## Alert thresholds

- **Warning** at **80%** used.
- **Page** at **90%** used.
- **Emergency** at **95%** used: stop all non-critical producers.

## First response

1. Find the largest topics: `du -sh /var/lib/kafka/* | sort -h | tail`.
2. Delete the oldest log segment files of the largest topic by hand.
3. If usage is still rising, expand the volume by **500 GiB**.

## Capacity review

Disk headroom is reviewed **quarterly** with the infrastructure team.

listeners-and-auth — Kafka Listeners and Client Authentication

# Kafka Listeners and Client Authentication

Version 3 · Effective 2026-02-01 · Owner: Streaming SRE

## Purpose

How applications connect to the production Kafka cluster and how they
authenticate.

## Client connection

- Bootstrap servers: `kafka.prod.halcyon.internal:9094`.
- Client listener: port **9094**, protocol **SASL_SSL**.
- SASL mechanism: **SCRAM-SHA-512**.
- Minimum TLS version: **1.3**.

## Inter-broker traffic

Brokers talk to each other on port **9093** using **SSL**.

## Credentials

- Client credentials are issued per application from Vault at `secret/kafka/clients/<app>`.
- Client certificates are rotated every **90 days**.

## Troubleshooting

`Connection to node -1 could not be established` almost always means the client
is pointed at the wrong port or protocol. Compare the client config with the
values above.

# Kafka Listeners and Client Authentication

Version 1 · Effective 2024-03-01 · Owner: Data Platform

## Purpose

How applications connect to the production Kafka cluster and how they
authenticate.

## Client connection

- Bootstrap servers: `kafka-prod.halcyon.internal:9092`.
- Client listener: port **9092**, protocol **PLAINTEXT**.
- SASL mechanism: **none (PLAINTEXT has no authentication)**.
- Minimum TLS version: **1.2**.

## Inter-broker traffic

Brokers talk to each other on port **9091** using **PLAINTEXT**.

## Credentials

- Client credentials are issued as the shared `svc-kafka` account; the password is on the team wiki.
- Client certificates are rotated every **365 days**.

## Troubleshooting

`Connection to node -1 could not be established` almost always means the client
is pointed at the wrong port or protocol. Compare the client config with the
values above.

oncall-escalation — Kafka On-Call Escalation Policy

# Kafka On-Call Escalation Policy

Version 3 · Effective 2026-06-01 · Owner: Streaming SRE

## Who is on call

The **Streaming SRE** team owns production Kafka incidents. Pages arrive through the
PagerDuty service **`streaming-platform-prod`**.

## Response times

- Primary acknowledges within **5 minutes**.
- No acknowledgement: escalate to the secondary after **15 minutes**.
- Not resolved: escalate to the engineering manager after **30 minutes**.

## SEV-1

Declare it with `/incident declare` in Slack, which opens the bridge, and post updates in **#inc-streaming** every 15 minutes.

## After the incident

Write the post-incident review within five working days.

chunks.text:
schema-registry — Kafka Schema Registry Operations

# Kafka Schema Registry Operations

Version 2 · Effective 2026-03-20 · Owner: Streaming SRE

## Endpoint

- URL: `https://schemas.prod.halcyon.internal:8085`.
- Port: **8085**.
- Authentication: **mutual TLS**.

## Compatibility

The default compatibility level is **FULL_TRANSITIVE**. Subjects use
`TopicNameStrategy`, so the subject for topic `orders.v1` is `orders.v1-value`.

## Registering schemas

Only the CI pipeline may register schemas. Services read schemas but never write them.

## Deleting schemas

Deleting a schema version is forbidden. Raise it with the Architecture Review Board.

# Kafka Schema Registry Operations

Version 1 · Effective 2024-07-15 · Owner: Data Platform

## Endpoint

- URL: `http://schema-registry.halcyon.internal:8081`.
- Port: **8081**.
- Authentication: **none**.

## Compatibility

The default compatibility level is **BACKWARD**. Subjects use
`TopicNameStrategy`, so the subject for topic `orders.v1` is `orders.v1-value`.

## Registering schemas

Any service may register a schema on first produce.

## Deleting schemas

Soft-delete a schema version with `DELETE /subjects/<subject>/versions/<n>`.

chunks.text:
topic-creation-standards — Kafka Topic Creation Standards

# Kafka Topic Creation Standards

Version 3 · Effective 2026-02-15 · Owner: Streaming SRE

## Purpose

Every new production topic must follow these standards so that capacity,
ownership and naming stay predictable.

## Naming

Topic names follow `<domain>.<team>.<dataset>.v<N>`, lowercase, dots as separators.
Example: `payments.ledger.transactions.v1`.

## Required settings

- Partitions: **12** by default.
- Replication factor: **3**.
- `min.insync.replicas`: **2**.
- Topics over **96** partitions need a capacity review.

## How to request a topic

Open a pull request in the `kafka-topics` Terraform repository. CI validates the name and settings.

## Not allowed

Auto-created topics are disabled on production (`auto.create.topics.enable=false`).

# Kafka Topic Creation Standards

Version 2 · Effective 2024-05-20 · Owner: Data Platform

## Purpose

Every new production topic must follow these standards so that capacity,
ownership and naming stay predictable.

## Naming

Topic names follow `<team>.<dataset>`, lowercase, dots as separators.
Example: `ledger.transactions`.

## Required settings

- Partitions: **6** by default.
- Replication factor: **3**.
- `min.insync.replicas`: **1**.
- Topics over **50** partitions need a capacity review.

## How to request a topic

Open a Jira ticket in the KAFKA project. The Data Platform team creates the topic by hand.

## Not allowed

Auto-created topics are disabled on production (`auto.create.topics.enable=false`).

chunks.heading: Kafka Topic Retention Policy
chunks.text:
topic-retention — Kafka Topic Retention Policy

# Kafka Topic Retention Policy

Version 3 · Effective 2026-01-15 · Owner: Streaming SRE

## Purpose

This policy sets how long data stays on production Kafka topics and who may
change it. Retention is the main lever on broker disk usage.

## Defaults for new topics

- `retention.ms` default: **259200000** (3 days).
- `retention.bytes` default: **53687091200 (50 GiB per partition)**.
- `cleanup.policy` default: `delete`. Compacted topics must say so explicitly.
- Compacted topics use `min.compaction.lag.ms` of **6 hours**.

## Changing retention

- Teams may set retention themselves up to **7 days**.
- Anything longer needs approval from **the Architecture Review Board**.
- Make the change with: `kctl topic set-retention <topic> --ms <value>`.
- Audit topics (prefix `audit.`) are kept for **180 days** and cannot be shortened.

## Verify

Describe the topic config after the change and confirm the value appears.

topic-retention-2024 — Kafka Topic Retention Policy

# Kafka Topic Retention Policy

Version 2 · Effective 2024-09-01 · Owner: Data Platform

## Purpose

This policy sets how long data stays on production Kafka topics and who may
change it. Retention is the main lever on broker disk usage.

## Defaults for new topics

- `retention.ms` default: **604800000** (7 days).
- `retention.bytes` default: **-1 (unlimited)**.
- `cleanup.policy` default: `delete`. Compacted topics must say so explicitly.
- Compacted topics use `min.compaction.lag.ms` of **1 hour**.

## Changing retention

- Teams may set retention themselves up to **14 days**.
- Anything longer needs approval from **Data Governance**.
- Make the change with: `kafka-configs.sh --alter --entity-type topics --entity-name <topic> --add-config retention.ms=<value>`.
- Audit topics (prefix `audit.`) are kept for **90 days** and cannot be shortened.

## Verify

Describe the topic config after the change and confirm the value appears.
